prompt.content: timeline_track world: replay events with read_event / read_events to compute the state of objects at a query time T.

Process the timeline at checkpoints [26, 72, 99, 165, 186]. For each checkpoint C, look only at events in the interval since the previous checkpoint (starting from 0 for the first interval) and find the actor who received the most TRANSFER actions in that interval. Count a TRANSFER for the actor in its `to` field; break ties by alphabetically earliest actor name. Also report how many non-destroyed objects that same actor owns at checkpoint C, after events with index < C have been applied. Submit JSON as [[checkpoint, actor, interval_transfer_count, owned_count_at_checkpoint], ...] in checkpoint order. You need to carry object ownership/existence forward across checkpoints but reset interval transfer counts after each checkpoint. Use read_event(i) or read_events(start, end) (capped at 5/call). OBJECTS, ACTORS, LOCATIONS, and N_EVENTS are pre-seeded.
